properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All five production start scripts in packages/cron (metrics, dagcargo-sizes, storage, delete-remote-pins, names) run their worker with NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, which disables certificate verification for every outgoing TLS connection the cron workers make — a live posture control, changeable here. This is the cron fleet's actual operational configuration, not a sample or comment.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency in root package-lock.json (hash.js@1.1.7, transitive via the elliptic/@noble stack). Ships SHA-1/SHA-2 implementations in the build; no direct application import found. Dependency inventory — presence, not use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency: crypto-js@4.1.1 (root) plus 3.3.0 pinned for the packages/api and packages/website workspaces. The MD5 module ships in the library regardless of use; no direct source import found in application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency: crypto-js@4.1.1 (root) plus 3.3.0 for packages/api and packages/website. SHA-1 module ships in the library; no direct source import found in application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared deps secp256k1@^4.0.1 and @noble/secp256k1@^1.3.0 (lockfile, part of the magic.link/Ethereum auth stack), plus the protobuf-generated KeyType enum literals in packages/api/src/utils/crypto/pb/keys.js ("Secp256k1"=2) used to marshal user auth keys. ECDSA over secp256k1 underpins magic.link DID-token auth — Shor-vulnerable, migration vendor-dependent (magic.link).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: evp_bytestokey@^1.0.0/^1.0.3 declared in package-lock.json (transitive, browser-crypto polyfill stack). OpenSSL EVP_BytesToKey single-round-MD5 KDF ships in the library; no direct application call found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1 is resolved in the root lockfile and ships RSA, PKCS, X.509 and TLS implementations; part of the shipped dependency inventory (the image carries these algorithms whether or not the application calls them). No direct RSA call site found in application code in this shard.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 is the API's live signing algorithm for content claims: env.js:248 instantiates the signer from the CONTENT_CLAIMS_PRIVATE_KEY environment key (ed25519.parse), and utils/crypto/ed25519.js is the API's own Ed25519 wrapper — libp2p Ed25519PublicKey marshal/unmarshal plus Cloudflare Workers WebCrypto verify via crypto.subtle.importKey/verify with the NODE-ED25519 algorithm. keys.js sites are the generated libp2p protobuf KeyType codec (Ed25519 branch). Also @noble/ed25519 (^1.5.1/^1.7.3) in

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: create-ecdh@4.0.0 is declared in the root lockfile (a crypto-browserify-style polyfill for crypto.createECDH). It ships ECDH key agreement in the dependency tree; no direct application call site found in this shard's files. Dependency inventory: presence is the question here — the image carries ECDH whether or not the app calls it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Correction: tweetnacl@1.0.3 IS actively used, not merely declared — packages/api/src/utils/crypto/ed25519.js:33 dynamically imports it ('const { default: nacl } = await import("tweetnacl")') as the Ed25519 signature-verify fallback when the WebCrypto NODE-ED25519 path is unavailable (i.e. outside the Cloudflare Workers runtime). So the Ed25519 verification chain this object describes runs on tweetnacl in Node contexts.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 declared (transitive via the secp256k1/magic.link stack). ECDSA ships in the library; the API's user auth path validates ECDSA-over-secp256k1 DID tokens through @magic-sdk/admin, so this primitive is live in the auth chain even though the app never imports elliptic directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@^1.0.3 is declared in packages/api/package.json and really imported by the API crypto layer (utils/crypto/ed25519.js falls back to nacl.sign.detached.verify outside the CloudFlare worker runtime). X25519 scalar multiplication is part of the shipped tweetnacl library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2@^3.0.17 (plus @types/pbkdf2 and two further pbkdf2 ^3.0.3 entries) is resolved in the root lockfile. PBKDF2 is post-quantum-irrelevant as a KDF (Grover only) but belongs in the dependency inventory; iteration counts matter only if an application call site exists — none found in this shard.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@^3.0.0 declared in package-lock.json (transitive). The scrypt KDF ships in the build; no direct application call found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: keccak@3.0.0 (SHA-3/Keccak implementation, typically pulled in by the secp256k1 ecosystem) is resolved in the root lockfile. Dependency inventory entry; SHA-3 itself is post-quantum-robust for preimages.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js@4.1.1 ships AES (plus DES/3DES/RC4 in the same package) and is resolved in the root lockfile. Dependency inventory: the build carries these implementations; no application AES call site found in this shard. Note crypto-js 4.1.1 predates its maintainership warnings and its RNG defaults are weak if used for key material.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: blake3-wasm@2.1.5 is resolved in the root lockfile (BLAKE3 hash implementation, commonly pulled via multiformats/iroh-style hashing). Dependency inventory entry; BLAKE3 is post-quantum-robust.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@^1.0.3 declared in packages/api/package.json; XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox ships in the library. Observed application use of tweetnacl is its Ed25519 sign/verify API, not secretbox — recorded as available-in-shipped-library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl is a direct dependency of packages/api (and resolved at 1.0.3 in the root lockfile); it supplies Ed25519 signatures and XSalsa20-Poly1305 secret-box encryption. Same library as the ALG-683d5cd2 (Ed25519 via tweetnacl) object. Dependency inventory — the shipped build carries these primitives.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency (root crypto-js 4.1.1; packages/api and packages/website 3.3.0). No import found in application source; the library's MD5/SHA-1/EVP_BytesToKey modules ship in the build regardless. Presence is the question this inventory answers; use is a finding-level question.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge is resolved in the root lockfile (1.3.1); it is the provider behind the RSA (ALG-589856a1) and X.509 (ALG-1847d707) objects and the likely engine for selfsigned@2.0.1. Dependency inventory: ships RSA, X.509, PKCS, TLS implementations whether or not the application calls them.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned@^2.x declared (with node-forge) in package-lock.json; generates self-signed X.509 certificates, typically for dev-server HTTPS; no direct application import found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X.509 support ships via node-forge@1.3.1 in the root lockfile (same library as LIB-fe0eb9a4 and ALG-589856a1; selfsigned@2.0.1 also builds on it). Dependency inventory — certificate generation/parsing available in the shipped tree; no application call site found in this shard.

properties.name: pqs:context
